rich_summary: Arjuna, enraged by the death of his son Abhimanyu, swears a terrible oath: if he does not kill Jayadratha in the next day's battle, he will accept the fate of the worst sinners and even enter blazing fire. He invokes a long catalogue of moral transgressions, declaring he will share their cursed destinies if he fails. After this vow, he stretches the Gandiva bow and Krishna sounds the conch Panchajanya, shaking the universe and filling the Pandava camp with triumphant roars. Hearing the uproar and learning of the vow, Jayadratha is overcome with terror and considers fleeing the Kuru camp. Duryodhana, however, reassures him that the greatest Kaurava warriors—Drona, Karna, Kripa, and many others—will surround and protect him. The scene heightens tension for the coming battle, framing Arjuna’s vow as both cosmic and inevitable.

highlight_spans.why: Arjuna begins his fierce oath, invoking dire spiritual consequences if he fails to avenge Abhimanyu.
Arjuna declares that if Jayadratha survives until sunset he will enter blazing fire, raising the stakes of the next day’s battle.
The cosmic reaction—Krishna blowing the Panchajanya and Arjuna stretching Gandiva—symbolizes divine support and the gravity of the vow.
Jayadratha’s fear is revealed as he laments before the Kuru kings, realizing Arjuna’s vow may be unstoppable.
Duryodhana reassures Jayadratha by listing the many powerful Kaurava warriors who will defend him the next day.

top_scenes.scene_text: Arjuna, blazing with fury, stretches the Gandiva while Krishna beside him blows the conch Panchajanya, its thunder shaking the heavens and the Pandava army roaring in response.
Jayadratha stands trembling in the Kuru assembly, pale and despairing as he begs the gathered kings for protection from Arjuna’s vow.
Duryodhana confidently gestures around the hall as he names the great warriors—Drona, Karna, Kripa, and others—who will form a living fortress around Jayadratha.
